summary: Crash when clicking "Presets" after setting the superflat preset with a non-existent biome
description: Crash when you click "Presets" after replacing the "minecraft:plains" to a non-existent biome in the superflat customization menu I was creating a world called "Nether" with Superflat, I replaced "minecraft:plains" to "minecraft:the_nether" to see if the piglins won t turn to zombified piglins, I clicked "Done" and clicked "Presets" again to see if "minecraft:the_nether" doesn t has turn onto "minecraft:plains" again, and The Game Crashed What I expected to happen was: When I click presets after replacing it, it should resets to default. What happened was: It crashed after I press presets. How to reproduce: Create a new world in Superflat click on Customize, after click on Presets replace the biome from "minecraft:plains" to a non-existent biome in the superflat customization menu after click on Done and Presets again and see if it crash(If you press cancel it won t crash)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a new world in Superflat mode.
3. Click on "Customize".
4. Click on "Presets".
5. Replace the biome from "minecraft:plains" to a non-existent biome in the superflat customization menu.
6. Click "Done".
7. Click on "Presets" again.
8. Observe that the game crashes after pressing "Presets".
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 1.16.2, 1.16.3 Release Candidate 1, 1.16.3, 1.16.4 Pre-release 1, 1.16.4 Pre-release 2, 1.16.4 Release Candidate 1, 1.16.4
Observed Behavior: When attempting to access the "Presets" option after modifying the superflat preset to include a non-existent biome, the game crashes. This issue occurs specifically when the player replaces "minecraft:plains" with a biome that does not exist, such as "minecraft:the_nether." The player was creating a world called "Nether" using the Superflat option and made the change to test whether piglins would transform into zombified piglins. After clicking "Done" and then selecting "Presets" again to verify that the previous biome had not reverted to "minecraft:plains," the game crashed. The expected behavior was for the presets to reset to the default settings without any issues. Instead, the game crashed upon pressing the "Presets" button. To replicate this bug, one should create a new world in Superflat mode, navigate to the customization menu, replace the biome from "minecraft:plains" to a non-existent biome, click "Done," and then click "Presets" again. If the player selects "Cancel" instead of "Done," the game does not crash.
Expected Behavior: When clicking the "Presets" button after customizing a superflat world by replacing "minecraft:plains" with a non-existent biome, the game should reset the biome selection to the default "minecraft:plains" without crashing. Instead of crashing, the game should allow players to return to the preset menu safely, enabling them to check their changes and make further adjustments as needed. This behavior would ensure a smoother user experience when customizing superflat worlds.
